items.headline: Trump waives most of new Russia sanctions law
items.summary: President Trump waived many of the sanctions and tariffs in a new law targeting Russia and Iran. Experts say the move eases pressure on Moscow and raises concerns about U.S. support for Ukraine.

items.headline: Trump's midterm travel tilts toward safe red states
items.summary: President Trump promised a blitz of swing districts but is visiting several states he won easily two years ago. NPR says the schedule signals a tougher electoral landscape for Republicans.

items.headline: Minnesota Senate candidates clash over fraud and affordability
items.summary: The major-party candidates for Minnesota's U.S. Senate seat met in an hourlong MPR News debate. Fraud, affordability and the effects of Trump administration policies were the main points of friction.

items.headline: Alaska emerges as a Senate battleground
items.summary: Alaska could be pivotal to Democrats' hopes of winning the Senate. In a debate, Sen. Dan Sullivan faced questions on fuel costs and Mary Peltola responded to allegations about her treatment of staff.

items.headline: Midterm ad spending tops $10 billion
items.summary: Campaign advertising spending this election cycle has passed $10 billion. The surge comes as many voters say they are struggling to afford groceries and gas.

items.headline: Israeli leaders rule out partnering with Arab-led parties
items.summary: Netanyahu and his main rivals say they will not form a coalition with any Arab-led party after the Oct. 27 election. That stance could leave the country facing prolonged political gridlock.

items.headline: South Africans press new cases over apartheid-era crimes
items.summary: More than three decades after apartheid ended, families of victims are still seeking justice. A new wave of legal efforts is pursuing truth, accountability and reparations.

items.headline: Climate remains central to the global economy, analysis argues
items.summary: A TIME commentary says climate change and clean energy still shape economic performance. It notes that the IMF and World Bank meetings focused largely on war, AI and debt.

items.headline: Foiled Hindu temple attack tied to online hate, leaders say
items.summary: Community leaders say a thwarted mass shooting at a large Hindu temple in suburban Chicago was fueled by years of hateful online rhetoric. They point to rising hostility toward Hindus and Indians on social media.

items.headline: OB-GYNs issue new menopause treatment guidelines
items.summary: The American College of Obstetricians and Gynecologists has updated its guidance on treating hot flashes, night sweats and insomnia. It is the group's first update on menopause symptoms since 2014.

digest.overview:
Hundreds of No Kings rallies took place across the country Saturday, this time urging people to vote early. Campaigning in Kentucky, President Trump backed Andy Barr for Senate and promised a $100 million Department of War investment in a Winchester drug plant if Republicans keep Congress. Secretary of State Marco Rubio called Trump's waiver of new Russia sanctions a 60-day pause as senators from both parties criticized it. In Orange County, the Norte Fire grew to 570 acres and damaged or destroyed six homes, while evacuation orders for Malibu's Bryson Fire were lifted. The administration is suing California to stop it counting about 20,000 mail ballots it says came from likely noncitizens. CENTCOM said U.S. forces helped 400 merchant ships through Hormuz in the past week.

Abroad, a large Ukrainian drone attack set fires at an oil terminal and an oil depot in St. Petersburg, after Russia launched 332 drones plus missiles at Ukraine overnight. Iran's foreign minister said Tehran's offer to reopen Hormuz within six days of U.S. acceptance is still on the table. Egypt said it would help defend Saudi Arabia against the Houthis if asked. A deadly incident and fire hit Canada's CFB Wainwright ahead of Monday's Alberta referendum. More than 550,000 people marched in France in cost-of-living protests that also reached Belgium, Italy and Portugal. North Korea said it tested an AI-guided torpedo system, South Korea's Democratic Party leader said talks have begun on impeaching the chief justice, and Japan's Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi sent an offering to Yasukuni Shrine. Hurricane Trudy, now Category 2, brought a hurricane warning to Mexico's coast from Manzanillo to Cabo Corrientes.

home.overview:
The Rays evened the ALCS at two games apiece with a 7–3 win in Cleveland, as Jonathan Aranda had three hits, Yandy Díaz hit a ninth-inning two-run homer and Nick Martinez allowed one run over 5⅓ innings. Game 5 is Sunday at 5 p.m. ET, and the winner meets the Brewers in a World Series that opens Friday in Milwaukee. NFL Week 6 kicks off with Texans–Jaguars in London at 9:30 a.m. ET; Lamar Jackson and Jalen Hurts are out, Tyler Huntley starts for Baltimore in Cleveland, and Cowboys–Packers is the Sunday night game. The Knicks waived Bruce Brown to keep James Wiseman before Tuesday's NBA opener.

Man City made it seven wins from seven, edging Ipswich 3–2 to go six points clear of Arsenal, while Chelsea, Liverpool and Aston Villa all won away. Barcelona won 5–2 at Real Betis for a record-equalling nine-win start in La Liga, Luis Díaz hit a hat-trick in Bayern's 6–1 rout of RB Leipzig, and PSG rallied to win 3–1 at Strasbourg. FC Seoul drew 2–2 with Gimcheon and can clinch the K League 1 title next Saturday, Suwon Samsung moved five clear in K League 2, and Messi scored twice in Inter Miami's 3–1 win at Atlanta. In the KBO, Kia beat LG 6–3 for a 2–0 first-round lead.

brief: Kia beat LG 6–3 in Game 2 in Gwangju to take a 2–0 lead in their best-of-five first-round series.
Kia scored five runs in the first inning, and LG starter Im Chan-kyu was pulled after retiring one batter.
Adam Oller pitched six innings for the win, and closer Jeon Sang-hyun struck out Lee Jae-won with the tying run at the plate.
The series moves to Jamsil for Game 3 on Tuesday at 6:30 p.m. KST, with the winner facing No. 2 Samsung.
